question: At present, each Member State sets its own criteria for waste to obtain ‘end-of-waste’ status. This status exempts waste from the onerous regulations governing waste transport. In the absence of harmonisation, the transport of waste intended for recovery is difficult and particularly time-consuming due to the administrative procedures that must be completed when it crosses the territory of other Member States for recovery. 1.

Does the Commission plan to propose European-level harmonisation of the criteria for ‘end-of-waste’ status, at least for strategic waste streams such as plastics, paper, textiles, etc., as is already the case for waste metal and glass?

If it does not intend to propose criteria for other sectors, does the Commission plan to introduce a principle of mutual recognition of ‘end-of-waste’ status, so that operators will no longer have to make separate applications in each Member State?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (30.1.2026) Article 6(1) of the Waste Framework Directive (WFD)1 sets out general conditions under which waste which has undergone a recycling or other recovery operation is considered to have reached end-of-waste (EoW) status. Whether to adopt specific EoW criteria is left to the discretion of each Member State.

However, according to Article 6(2), the Commission shall monitor the development of national EoW criteria in Member States and assess the need to establish Union-wide EoW criteria. In line with Article 6(2) of the WFD and with the Circular Economy Action Plan2, the Commission published in 2022 a study3 to set a list of priority waste streams for which to develop Union-wide EoW criteria.

The identified top five priority streams are: plastics, textiles, rubber, mineral fractions of construction and demolition waste (CDW), and paper and cardboard. Building on that study, the Commission started working on technical proposals for Unionwide EoW criteria for plastics, textiles, and CDW.

The report on the technical proposals for plastic waste was published in November 20244, while the ones for textiles and for CDW are planned for publication in the course of 2026. In its Communication of 23 December 20255, the Commission announced the forthcoming adoption of an implementing regulation laying down Union-wide EoW criteria for plastic waste6.

The work for adopting implementing acts laying down Union wide EoW criteria for textiles and CDW is likely to start after the publication of the planned reports with the technical proposals. New measures to simplify the adoption of Union-wide EoW criteria are being considered and assessed under the forthcoming Circular Economy Act, expected to be adopted in the second half of 2026.
1 Directive 2008/98/EC of the European Parliament and of the Council of 19 November 2008 on waste and

repealing certain Directives, OJ L 312, 22.11.2008, p. 3–30. 2 https://environment.ec.europa.eu/strategy/circular-economy_en. 3 https://publications.jrc.ec.europa.eu/repository/handle/JRC128647. 4 https://publications.jrc.ec.europa.eu/repository/handle/JRC139303.

5 Communication from the Commission to the European Parliament, the Council, the European Economic and Social Committee and the Committee of the Regions - Accelerating Europe’s transition to a circular economy: a pilot for boosting the circularity of plastics, COM/2025/805 final. 6 The draft act is open for public feedback from 23 December 2025 to 26 January 2026 on Have our say https://ec.europa.
